title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-11
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 새 봉제 관리자 첫 출근(06:35 픽업·준비 목록 확인), 본사 지시대로 기존 기준 보험 재견적 요청 후 송부, 기계 교체 상사 결정 확인. 시험 채점 없음(화요일 실행)
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Tomorrow is Wednesday, November eleventh. This is your English briefing for Wednesday.

Today was a long day. You sent a safety status to head office. You sent the insurance renewal report. You reported a machine history to my director. You also started a big data collection from all teams. Tomorrow, a new manager starts work, and head office wants a new insurance quote. Let's get ready together.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for tomorrow. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a short practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for tomorrow.
Number one. A new quote for the fire insurance.

What is it? This afternoon, you sent the fire insurance renewal report to a head office manager. In the new plan, we changed the basis for the machines. Because of this, the premium went up. A premium is the money we pay for insurance. Late in the afternoon, the head office manager replied. The manager wants to keep the same basis as the current contract for machines. So the broker must make a new quote.

Why is it important? The current policy ends on December fifteenth. Head office must report to the CEO one month before it ends. The head office manager asked for the report by November eleventh, which is tomorrow. Also, my director asked why we changed the basis this year. He wants a realistic number.

Your first action tomorrow. Send a short request to the broker in the morning. Ask for a new quote with the same machine basis as the current contract. Ask for both the six month option and the one year option. Ask the accountant to check the asset list for the old basis. When you get the quote, send it to the head office manager with two options, as the manager suggested.
Number two. The new sewing manager's first day.

What is it? The new sewing manager is our new sewing manager from abroad. He arrived in the city today. Tomorrow is his first working day. The pickup is at six thirty-five in the morning. This morning, you sent a new joiner checklist to the purchasing staff, the HR manager, the IT staff and the accountant.

Why is it important? The first day leaves a strong picture in his mind. He has worked in Vietnam before, but his Vietnamese is not strong. If his desk, his email, or his papers are not ready, he will feel lost. Also, the sewing team has had no manager for some days, so the factory needs him soon.

Your first action tomorrow. Check the pickup at six thirty-five. Then walk him to his desk and check the checklist with each person. The purchasing staff has the desk and stationery. The IT staff has the laptop and email. The HR manager has the labor contract and papers. The accountant has the bank account. Then introduce him to the factory manager and the line leaders.
Number three. The fusing machine decision.

What is it? Today, you sent my director and the production head a report on the fusing machine. You listed the past repairs, the last belt change, and the price of a new machine. The machine is old. It still works, but the heat is not even on both sides.
Why is it important? If the machine stops, cutting and fusing will stop, and the lines will wait. But a new machine is a big cost. My director needs to choose: repair again, or buy a new one.

Your first action tomorrow. Ask my director if he has any questions on the report. If he wants a new machine, ask the purchasing staff to get quotations on the same terms. If he wants to repair, ask the compliance officer to check the belt and the heat again.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the warehouse staff. The stock count corrections items one and three were due on November ninth. Item two and the photos of the shared fabric records were due today. You have reminded the warehouse staff three times. Tomorrow, ask for a clear date. Here is a sentence you can use. "Excuse me, if you cannot finish today, please let me know the reason and the date you can finish."

Second, the purchasing staff. Today she sent the sample room air conditioner quote. She also sent the broken units and the repair history. You asked her three things. Get one more supplier, so there are three quotes. Attach the original quotes. And check if the installation work is included. Here is a sentence you can use. "Hi, please ask all three suppliers to quote the same scope, including installation."
The purchasing staff also still owes the October electricity VAT invoices. Ask about them in the same message.

Third, the maintenance staff and the production consumables. You approved the list today after two questions. Tomorrow is Wednesday, so the weekly consumables report goes to head office. Here is a sentence you can use. "Hi, please send the weekly report to head office today, and copy me."

Fourth, the compliance officer and the camera hard drives. You agreed to replace the camera hard drives before the audit. The compliance officer will work with the IT staff and get quotes from two suppliers on the same terms. Here is a sentence you can use. "Hi, when can I expect the two quotations?"

Fifth, all team leaders and the production data list. You sent the request today. The deadline is Saturday, November fourteenth. Each team must add missing forms to the list and upload one latest sample file. Tomorrow, open the list and see which teams have started. Here is a sentence you can use. "Just a reminder, the deadline is this Saturday. Please add your forms to the list today if you can."

Sixth, the export staff. You asked her to check the new trucking price from the trucking company. You want the old and new prices, the road ban, and when the ban will end. The deadline is Thursday, November twelfth.
Part three. Replies I owe.

First, a head office manager. The head office manager asked for a new quote with the old machine basis. Reply tomorrow morning with a short note. A good first sentence is: "Thank you for your guidance. I will ask the broker for a new quote with the current basis and send it to you as soon as I get it."

Second, my director about the fire insurance. My director asked why we changed the basis. You already explained it today. Now, tell him the head office decision. A good first sentence is: "Head office decided to keep the current basis for machines, so I asked the broker for a new quote."

Third, the interpreter and the overtime request for next week, November sixteenth to twenty-first. My director registers the overtime himself, so this is for your reference. Just open the file and check the hours are within the legal limit. A good first sentence, only if needed, is: "Hi, thank you. Please check line three. The hours look higher than last week."
Fourth, the daily worker status report. She sent it to my director and you this afternoon. No reply is needed. Just check the absence numbers before the morning meeting.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Tomorrow, Wednesday. Pick up the new sewing manager at six thirty-five, and his first day. The fire insurance report to head office is due. The accountant's revised fire insurance plan is due. The needle order goes for CEO approval. The weekly consumables report goes to head office.

Thursday, November twelfth. The weekly overtime report. The export staff's answer on the trucking price. The tax adviser's answer on the transfer pricing report. And one team leader comes back to work, so check the HR system update.
Friday, November thirteenth. The chief accountant's follow-up on transfer pricing, the weekly cash report, and the weekly outsourcing report.
Saturday, November fourteenth. The production data collection deadline for all teams.
Part five. English review.
Let's review expressions from the last week. There are eleven today. Listen first, then say each one out loud, slowly and clearly.
The expression is "overdue". It means late, after the deadline. For example, "Number one and number three are now overdue, so please finish them today." Now say it with me.
One more time. Number one and number three are now overdue, so please finish them today.
The expression is "scope". It means the range of the work. For example, "Please ask all three companies to quote the same scope." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please ask all three companies to quote the same scope.

The expression is "If you cannot ..., please let me know the reason and the date you can ...". You use it when someone may miss a deadline. For example, "If you cannot finish number two today, please let me know the reason and the date you can finish." Now say it with me.
One more time. If you cannot finish number two today, please let me know the reason and the date you can finish.

The expression is "A says ..., whereas B says ...". You use it to show that two things do not match. For example, "The current contract says one basis, whereas the new quote says another." Now say it with me.
One more time. The current contract says one basis, whereas the new quote says another.
The expression is "pending". It means until something is decided. For example, "Pending my director's decision, please do not order a new belt." Now say it with me.
One more time. Pending my director's decision, please do not order a new belt.

The expression is "... will take over ..., while you continue to ...". You use it to split work between two people. For example, "the new sewing manager will take over the sewing lines, while you continue to handle line balancing." Now say it with me.
One more time. The new sewing manager will take over the sewing lines, while you continue to handle line balancing.
The expression is "It turned out that ...". It means "I found out later that ...". For example, "It turned out that last year's contract did not cover all the machines." Now say it with me.
One more time. It turned out that last year's contract did not cover all the machines.
The expression is "I would appreciate it if you could ...". It is a polite way to ask. For example, "I would appreciate it if you could send the new quote by noon." Now say it with me.
One more time. I would appreciate it if you could send the new quote by noon.
The expression is "prompt". It means quick, without delay. For example, "Thank you for your prompt reply. The new quote is very helpful." Now say it with me.
One more time. Thank you for your prompt reply. The new quote is very helpful.

The expression is "oversee". It means to watch and manage something as the person in charge. For example, "From tomorrow, the new sewing manager will oversee all the sewing lines." Now say it with me.
One more time. From tomorrow, the new sewing manager will oversee all the sewing lines.
The expression is "Going forward, please ...". It means "from now on, please ...". For example, "Going forward, please use the same machine basis for every insurance renewal." Now say it with me.
One more time. Going forward, please use the same machine basis for every insurance renewal.
Part six. A short role-play.
It is six fifty in the morning. Anthony meets the new sewing manager at the office on his first day.
Anthony: Good morning, the new sewing manager. Welcome to the city. Did you sleep well?
New manager: Good morning, Anthony. Yes, thank you. The apartment is quiet.
Anthony: Good. First, let me show you your desk. The purchasing staff prepared your chair and stationery.
New manager: Thank you. When can I get my laptop and email?
Anthony: The IT staff will set them up this morning. If anything is missing, please tell me directly.
New manager: OK. And the papers for my work permit?
Anthony: The HR manager will help you with the labor contract and the work permit papers. Please bring your passport to her office at nine.
New manager: Sure. When can I see the sewing lines?
Anthony: Right after that. The factory manager will walk you through the lines and introduce the line leaders.
New manager: Great. Is there anything I should know about the lines now?

Anthony: Yes. We have new styles on some lines, and efficiency is low at the start. For now, please just watch and listen. Next week, I would appreciate it if you could share your first ideas with my director.
New manager: No problem. Thank you for your help.
Anthony: You're welcome. Welcome to the team.
Part seven. Let's practice three key sentences from the role-play.
Sentence one. "If anything is missing, please tell me directly." Now say it with me.
One more time. If anything is missing, please tell me directly.
Sentence two. "the factory manager will walk you through the lines and introduce the line leaders." Now say it with me.
One more time. The factory manager will walk you through the lines and introduce the line leaders.
Sentence three. "For now, please just watch and listen." Now say it with me.
One more time. For now, please just watch and listen.
Part eight. Closing.

Tomorrow has one main job. Welcome the new sewing manager well, and get the new fire insurance quote with the old machine basis to the head office manager. After that, check the warehouse corrections, the purchasing staff's three quotes, and the team data list.
You did a lot today. Tomorrow, keep it simple: first the people, then the numbers.
Have a good evening, Anthony. See you tomorrow morning.
